answer_raw:
The **train** is the superior choice for most travelers due to lower door-to-door friction and more efficient city-center access.

| Feature | Train (Amtrak) | Flight (Commercial) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Door-to-Door Time** | **~3.5–4 hours** [2] | **~3h 45m–5h 30m** [4] |
| **Typical Cost** | **$20–$150** [2][3] | **$425+** (per AA, 11/09/26) [6] |

The train journey typically takes about **3.5 to 4 hours** [2]. While the flight itself is only about **1 hour and 5 minutes** [4], the total door-to-door time is often longer due to airport access, security, and transfers, typically landing between **3h 45m and 5h 30m** [4].

Costs vary wildly based on how far in advance you book. Amtrak tickets can range from **$20** (per Night Owl fares, undated) to **$150** [2][3]. For flights, a specific booking for November 9, 2026, shows prices starting at **$425** via American Airlines [6].

I would pick the **train** because the lack of TSA checkpoints and the ability to travel from city center to city center makes the transit time more predictable and often shorter than flying [8].
